Teaching Media & Technology

Teaching media and technology — projected aids, video, computers, e-learning and telehealth for nursing education.

🎯 After this chapter you can

  • Select teaching media appropriate to learners
  • Describe projected and non-projected aids
  • Explain computer-assisted and e-learning
  • Use telehealth in nursing education

In simple words

Media are the aids a teacher uses to make a lesson visible, clear and memorable. Choose the medium that suits the audience, the setting and the message.

Projected aids

Aid Best for
Chalkboard and whiteboard Fast, low-cost teaching
Slides Large groups and large diagrams
Overhead projector Overlays and transparency sheets
Video and films Procedures, animation, patient interviews
Computer with projector Interactive learning and PowerPoint sessions

Non-projected aids

Aid Best for
Charts and posters Low-literacy groups and clinics
Models and specimens Anatomy and physiology teaching
Flash cards Very small groups
Flip charts Mobile community teaching
Puppets Children as learners or as an audience
Printed handouts Reinforcement of key points
Real objects Familiarity (specimen of a food item)

Digital tools for nursing education

  • E-learning — modules, discussion forums, quizzes
  • Webinars — distance lectures across sites
  • Simulation and virtual reality labs — safe practice for emergencies
  • Electronic records and hospital information system — practice documentation
  • Telehealth — patient counselling, triage and follow-up teaching
  • Chatbots and knowledge apps — revision and quick answers

Selecting media — rules

  1. It must match the learning objective
  2. The audience must be able to see and read it
  3. It must work in the setting (power, room size, light)
  4. It must be affordable and reusable
  5. It must be prepared in advance and checked

🔴 Media support teaching, they do not replace it

the teacher is the most important teaching aid. Use media to make the point visible, then practice, question and discuss.

🔴 Most important for exams

  1. Choose media that match the objective and the learner.
  2. Projected aids: chalkboard, slides, video, projector.
  3. Non-projected aids: charts, models, flash cards, objects.
  4. E-learning and webinars allow distance nursing education.
  5. Simulation labs provide safe practice.

⭐ Important for exams

  1. Video is ideal for demonstrating procedures.
  2. Charts and posters suit low-literacy community audiences.
  3. Telehealth supports counselling and follow-up teaching.
  4. Always check equipment and lighting before class.
  5. Printed handouts reinforce key points.

📌 Memory trick

Media choice: A-L-A-H — Aim, Learner, Availability, Handling cost.

60-second revision

  • Projected aids: board, slides, video, computer projector.
  • Non-projected aids: charts, models, flash cards, handouts.
  • Digital: e-learning, webinars, simulation, telehealth.
  • Media must aim, suit the audience, work in the setting and be affordable.
  • The teacher remains the most important aid.

Test yourself

Which aid is best for teaching a procedure with animation?

Answer: B. Video can show animated procedures step by step and is ideal for skill teaching.

A poster set is best suited for:

Answer: A. Posters communicate visually to audiences who may not read well and are cheap and portable.

A simulation laboratory provides:

Answer: B. Simulation labs allow practice of emergencies safely before real patient care.

Telehealth in nursing education supports:

Answer: B. Telehealth supports counselling, triage and follow-up teaching over distance.

The most important teaching aid is:

Answer: B. Media support teaching, but the teacher’s communication, feedback and judgement are central.
